analysis.description: The paper explores the impact of various sources of variance in machine learning benchmarks, such as data sampling and hyperparameter choices. It reveals that these variances significantly affect benchmarking outcomes. The study demonstrates that incorporating more variation sources leads to a better approximation of the ideal estimator with reduced compute cost. Recommendations for performance comparisons across multiple deep learning tasks are provided based on these findings.

type.justification: The paper performs empirical evaluations to understand variance sources in machine learning benchmarks and uses experiments to support its conclusions.
type.quote: This study leads us to propose recommendations for performance comparisons.

name.justification: The paper primarily discusses benchmarking processes and variances within machine learning algorithms, placing it within the broader field of Machine Learning.
name.quote: We model the whole benchmarking process, revealing that variance due to data sampling, parameter initialization and hyperparameter choice impact markedly the results.
